about.title: Just sit for a while.
about.body: Pick today's social battery, then chat with a stranger for 7 minutes. If you both want to, you can stay longer. You can leave any time. This page is an interactive prototype, and matching and replies are simulated by the program.
about.bodyLive: Pick today's social battery, then chat with a stranger for 7 minutes. If you both want to, you can stay longer. You can leave any time and report anything that makes you uncomfortable. During the beta only adults can join. Ordinary chats and both profiles are deleted when the conversation ends, and the chat screen is cleared. Submit reports before the conversation ends; report evidence is kept for 180 days for review.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: LowBatteryTown ("we") is an anonymous one-to-one chat with no sign-up. This page explains what we handle, why, and for how long.

p: There is no account. We don't collect your real name, e-mail, phone number or social handles.
Please don't share anything that identifies you. Links, e-mail addresses, @handles and phone numbers are masked automatically before a message is sent.
Anonymous guest code: issued to your browser when you enter, kept in the browser's localStorage and valid for {tokenHours} hours, so a refresh or dropped connection can rejoin your chat.
Nickname, social battery and chat intent: shown to the person you are paired with.

Messages and pairing profiles: temporarily stored during an active chat for reconnects. When either person leaves, the session expires or the reconnect window runs out, they are immediately deleted from application chat storage and cleared from browsers that receive the end event. Reports cannot be submitted after the chat ends.
IP address: used only for abuse rate limits, as short-lived counters (about an hour at most), never stored with chat content.
Reports: when someone reports a chat we keep that conversation, both nicknames/batteries/intents, the reason and any note for safety review, and delete them after {reportDays} days.
Technical logs: server error and access logs (which may include IP and time) for operations and debugging.
Usage statistics: if we enable Google Analytics, it uses cookies for anonymous browsing statistics; you can block them in your browser.

Safety review: an anonymous guest code can be suspended from matching for 24 hours or 7 days after report review. Restrictions expire; reasons, durations and revocation history are retained with report evidence for {reportDays} days. No device fingerprint or real-identity profile is created.
To pair people and relay chats, to prevent abuse and handle reports, and to keep the service running. We don't sell data or use chats for advertising.

Cloudflare provides computing and data storage, and data may be processed outside Taiwan. Deletion above refers to application chat storage. Infrastructure backup or recovery systems may have separate retention periods; deletion does not mean all technical records disappear at the same instant.

Under Taiwan's Personal Data Protection Act you may ask to access, correct or delete your data. Because the service is anonymous we usually can't tell who you are; include the approximate time and your nickname when you write and we'll do our best.
During the beta the town is for people aged 18 and over.
We'll post material changes on this page and update the effective date.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By entering the town you agree to these terms and the community guidelines.

p: LowBatteryTown pairs two anonymous people for a 7-minute chat, extended only when both agree. It is a beta: features and opening hours may change or pause, and a partner isn't always available.
You must be 18 or older.
Follow the community guidelines. If you don't, we may end chats, pause pairing or restrict your use.
You are responsible for your messages. You let us process them as needed to relay them and to handle reports.
The town is not counselling or medical care. In immediate danger call 110 or 119 (Taiwan); for someone to listen, call 1925 or 1995.

"Light a lamp" is a one-off, voluntary contribution (NT$60 / 150 / 300). Nothing recurs and free chatting doesn't change. Payments are not open yet; before they open we will publish the operator's details and payment/refund terms.
The service is provided as is. Each person is responsible for their own conduct; we act on reports but, as far as the law allows, make no promise about what others say or who they are.
These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of China (Taiwan), with the Taiwan Taipei District Court as the court of first instance.

guidelines.title: Community guidelines
guidelines.intro: The town is a place to rest when your social battery is low. A few things keep it safe and easy:

p: Slow replies are fine. Don't rush, pry or demand an answer.
No sexual content or innuendo, hate, threats, bullying or discrimination.
Don't ask for or share phone numbers, addresses, schools, workplaces or social accounts. Links, e-mails, @handles and phone numbers are masked automatically.
No ads, no pulling people to other platforms, no asking for money for any reason.
If someone says they are under 18, end the chat and report it.

sections.h: Leave when it doesn't feel right
p: You can say good night any time. Reporting ends the chat at once, you won't be paired again for 24 hours, and the conversation is kept for review.
In Taiwan, 1925 and 1995 answer around the clock; in immediate danger call 110 or 119.

sections.h: What happens if rules are broken
p: We may end chats or restrict pairing; where the law or someone's safety requires it, we may cooperate with the authorities.

guide.title: Anonymous Chat Guide and Frequently Asked Questions
guide.description: Learn how free, no-sign-up anonymous chat works at LowBatteryTown: real-person matching, social battery, 7-minute conversations, waiting, privacy and reporting.
guide.intro: LowBatteryTown is a free, one-on-one anonymous chat website with no sign-up. Choose a nickname and your current social battery, then sit with someone who also wants to talk. You do not need to exchange contact details, and you can leave whenever you like.

questions.q: Do I need an account or payment?
questions.a: No account is needed and chatting is free. Use a nickname for this visit; payments are currently unavailable. The beta is for people aged 18 or older. Before entering, confirm the terms, community guidelines and privacy policy.
Nearly empty, a little left, and ready to talk describe your current pace. Your partner can see your battery and chat preference. Your battery is not a score or an identity.

questions.q: How do I match with a real person? What if nobody is waiting?
questions.a: Choose your nickname, battery and chat preference, confirm you are 18 or older, then enter the town. Matching requires another suitable real person to be waiting. Online visitors are not necessarily waiting, and immediate matching is not guaranteed. You can cancel waiting. If a companion is online, you may receive an invitation showing their nickname; chatting starts only if you accept.

questions.q: How long can we chat? Can I leave early?
questions.a: The first conversation lasts 7 minutes. It continues only if both people agree to extend it. You can say good night and leave at any time, without explaining why.

questions.q: Is my partner a real person or AI?
questions.a: The live town pairs real people. Companion invitations show the other person’s nickname and require your acceptance. The demo uses a clearly labelled simulated partner so you can try the flow.

questions.q: Does anonymous mean no records? Can screenshots be prevented?
questions.a: When an ordinary chat ends, the application immediately deletes its messages and both pairing profiles, and clears browsers that receive the end event. Evidence reported during a chat is kept for 180 days for review. Anonymous guest tokens, abuse-prevention counters and technical logs follow separate rules in the privacy policy. A website cannot reliably prevent screenshots or photos. Avoid sharing names, phone numbers, addresses or other identifying information.

questions.q: What if someone harasses me or makes me uncomfortable?
questions.a: You can leave at any time or report the conversation. Reporting ends the chat, saves its transcript for review and prevents the pair from matching again for 24 hours. The town is not counselling or an emergency service. If you are in immediate danger, contact local emergency services.
